title: Make packaging fail-closed, and stop backups carrying what was scrubbed

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 9128abd on main; working tree clean apart from .vscode/settings.json. Sprint file read fresh.

This is the sprint where a passing test suite proves the least, because Req 1 changes the mechanism that produces the artifact every other check runs against. So I built real tarballs and installed them, rather than reading the array.

================================================================
REQ 1 — DERIVED FROM install.js, RE-DERIVED BY ME FROM THE SAME SOURCE
================================================================

The criterion says a review that only compares the array against a directory listing has not verified this. So I built the required set from the installer's own path lists first, then compared:

  FRAMEWORK_OWNED   .claude/commands, scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py, scripts/run-lifecycle.js,
                    scripts/smoke_test.sh, scripts/dev2_worktree.sh, scripts/worktree_test.sh,
                    scripts/launcher, scripts/install.js, templates/sprint-template.md,
                    docs/HUMAN_OVERRIDE.md
  USER_OWNED        .claude/agents, CLAUDE.md, docs/sprints
  SPRINT_SKELETON   the seven docs/sprints/*/.gitkeep
  BASELINES_PATH    scripts/baselines/user-owned-content.json
  line 852          scripts/launcher/generate-tasks.js  (inside scripts/launcher)
  line 258          package.json                        (npm ships it regardless)

Every one is covered by the `files` array. Nothing the installer reads is missing.

REQ 1b — the two additions beyond that set are both noted as such, in the installer's own header where Req 1a asks the reasoning to live. CHANGELOG.md is consumer-facing and never opened by install.js. scripts/baselines ships wholesale rather than just the JSON, and I checked that justification rather than accepting it: scripts/verify-tarball.sh line 144 really does run `node "$UNPACKED/scripts/baselines/check-staleness.js"` — from the unpacked tarball, not this repo's source — and that script requires generate.js in turn. Omitting either would have left an installed project fine and silently broken Pipeman's own release-verification step on the next publish. That is a real dependency found by building, exactly as Req 1b asks, and shipping the directory rather than three named files is the right call for the same reason the array exists at all.

================================================================
REQ 1a — BOTH CLAIMS PROVEN WITH REAL TARBALLS, NOT PRECEDENCE REASONING
================================================================

The requirement forbids settling this by reasoning, and both halves are load-bearing, so I ran both against real, non-dry-run `npm pack` output in a copy of the repo:

  .npmignore does NOT filter inside a directory `files` lists wholesale
    added `scripts/launcher/jsonc.js` to .npmignore, packed
    -> jsonc.js SHIPPED anyway.  Claim holds.

  a `files` array is a complete allowlist on its own
    deleted .npmignore entirely, planted docs/sprints/state/sprint-999.json, packed
    -> sprint-999.json did NOT ship; docs/sprints held exactly the seven .gitkeep.

The second one is the one that matters and it is the whole design. With no denylist present at all, this repository's own sprint content is structurally unable to ship, because docs/sprints is never listed as a directory — only the seven placeholders install.js actually reads, individually. That is fail-closed by construction rather than by anyone remembering to add a pattern, which is the exact defect the Context describes: every .npmignore entry past the original three was added after someone noticed something would otherwise ship.

Keeping .npmignore as an inert, documented note was right. Deleting it would have left the next person to rediscover both findings from scratch.

REQ 5 — THE REAL TARBALL, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Packed 0.2.8 and inspected it:

  docs/sprints/ in the tarball:  exactly seven .gitkeep files, nothing else
  leak grep (settings.local, registry.json, state/*.json, disclosure docs, .vscode, .git):  nothing
  every path install.js needs:   all 15 present
  56 entries total

And the check the criteria added this round — "contains every path install.js needs" — I did not stop at the file list. I unpacked the tarball and ran a real fresh install into a scratch git repo: .claude/commands (15 files), .claude/agents (6), scripts/launcher (12), templates (1), docs/sprints (7), plus sprint_lifecycle.py, run-lifecycle.js and HUMAN_OVERRIDE.md. Then ran the installed framework in place — `sprint_lifecycle.py list` and `run-lifecycle.js list` both work from the target. An under-inclusive allowlist is the risk that packs cleanly and breaks someone's project; this one doesn't.

================================================================
REQS 2 AND 3 — RUN, NOT READ
================================================================

Same scratch target, seeded first with a .gitignore holding two unrelated lines and a planted `scripts/session.js.fc-bak-0.2.5` this run would never create. After the install:

  .gitignore:
    node_modules/
    my-own-secret.env
                                     <- both preserved (Req 2a)
    # Fully Completely (added by scripts/install.js)
    docs/sprints/.locks/
    *.fc-bak-*                       <- Req 2

  Backup files present, from any past upgrade (report only, nothing deleted) (1):
    scripts/session.js.fc-bak-0.2.5  <- Req 3b: a PRE-EXISTING backup, from a version
                                        this run never touched, which is the entire
                                        population the requirement exists for

  the planted file afterwards:  still on disk, content intact  <- Req 3a

REQ 3a, THE STRUCTURAL HALF — grepped the diff for any added deletion: none. The only `fs.unlinkSync` in install.js is pre-existing, at line 550 in removeStaleFrameworkFile(), and it removes the stale framework file AFTER copying it to a backup. Nothing in this file ever unlinks a `.fc-bak-` path. The requirement is satisfied by there being no such code, not by a flag.

THE CRLF FIX — not scope creep, and I verified it does what it claims rather than taking the explanation. Installed into a target whose .gitignore was pure CRLF and which needed only the new line appended:

  result: 5 CRLF, 0 bare LF

Before the fix that append joined with a bare '\n' and would have mixed endings in a file this installer had just written. removeDeadGitignoreLines() two functions above already did this detection; this was the second instance of a bug already found and fixed once here. Fixing it inside install.js is within Req 6's boundary, and leaving it would have meant knowingly shipping a file-corrupting-ish write that your own Req 2 change had just made reachable.

REQ 4 — npm's latest is 0.2.7, package.json is 0.2.8. Confirmed at audit time rather than trusted from the sprint file, which is what the requirement asks.

REQ 6 — the diff is exactly .npmignore, package.json, scripts/install.js. No lifecycle script, no CLAUDE.md, no agent file.

SUITE: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED (run by me, as the criteria require), TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED "Installed 0.2.8", ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, ALL WORKTREE TESTS PASSED.

ON "NO TESTS ADDED" — correct here, and I checked rather than reflexively objecting. Req 6 confines the diff to three files, launcher_test.js is not among them, and the two things worth asserting mechanically (the tarball's contents, an install from it) are already covered by verify-tarball.sh, which the criteria have QA1 and Pipeman both run. What you did instead — a real upgrade from the published 0.2.7 and a hand cross-check of the packed listing — is the verification that actually fits this change. I would have pushed back if the allowlist had shipped with nothing but a green suite behind it; it didn't.

CARRIED, INFORMATIONAL
- The allowlist's completeness is now a property of two lists in two files agreeing: `files` in package.json and FRAMEWORK_OWNED/USER_OWNED/SPRINT_SKELETON_FILES in install.js. Nothing mechanically checks that they still agree, so a future path added to the installer can drop out of the package silently — the same class of drift sprints 30 and 31 built the args-derivation protection for. verify-tarball.sh would catch it only if the missing path happens to break the install it runs. Worth its own small sprint: a check that every FRAMEWORK_OWNED/USER_OWNED entry is covered by `files`. Not a defect in this sprint, which does exactly what it was asked.
- The version-bump line is present in this sprint's Requirements (Req 4) — first time in six sprints. Whatever changed in the template, it worked.
- Long-carried: every launcher allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 35, Pipeman ships 9128abd and publishes 0.2.8.

For LiveQA: the fresh install into a clean scratch directory is the criterion this sprint most endangers, and it is not the same test as an upgrade — an under-inclusive allowlist publishes cleanly and then breaks someone's project. Do it from the registry, not from a local tarball. Plant an unrelated .gitignore line AND a `*.fc-bak-<old>` file before upgrading, then confirm the report names the backup and the file is still on disk afterwards; a report that quietly deletes fails Req 3a. And check `gitHead` against `last_shipped_commit` from `npm view`, not from Pipeman's handoff.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.2.8 with real installs into clean scratch repos. Environment: macOS Darwin arm64, 2026-09-10. No billed agent runs — every check here is a packaging or install-behaviour property.

PROVENANCE
0.2.8 on the registry; dist-tags.latest 0.2.8; gitHead 7d98cc9bef72d9ed19e0e7d929cc3cf213898519 == last_shipped_commit; zero `reshipped` events. Content check per sprint 13's rule: all 56 published files byte-identical to `git show 7d98cc9:<path>`, MISMATCHED 0, NOT-IN-COMMIT 0, tarball sha1 37d40bcd... matches the registry's dist.shasum.

PIPEMAN'S SHIP-COMMIT SUBSTITUTION — CHECKED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED. Dev Team's handoff named 9128abd; Pipeman shipped 7d98cc9. I verified the claim myself instead of taking it: `git diff 9128abd 7d98cc9` touches exactly one path, docs/sprints/state/sprint-35.json, and nothing else. That is bookkeeping, and SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS exempts `docs/sprints/state/*.json` by design, so the ship-hash gate passed on merit rather than being routed around. QA1 audited 9128abd; the code QA1 audited is byte-for-byte the code that shipped.

Worth recording because it is the first time I have seen it fire in a real ship: /sprint-ship refused 9128abd for having zero CI runs, and Pipeman did not route around it. That is sprint 28's split of the undeterminable-CI case working in the field, on a live release, rather than in a constructed test.

================================================================
THE 63 -> 56 DROP — ENUMERATED, NOT WAVED THROUGH
================================================================
Pipeman flagged the file count falling from 63 to 56 as needing eyes, and was right to: an under-inclusive `files` array is the one failure here that packs, publishes and verifies cleanly and then breaks someone's project. I diffed the two tarballs rather than accepting "expected for a fail-closed sprint". Seven files dropped, nothing added:

  .github/workflows/scan.yml          docs/sprint-12-permission-scope-findings.md
  .vscode/settings.json               scripts/launcher_test.js
  .vscode/tasks.json                  scripts/permission-gate-repro.js
  scripts/verify-tarball.sh

Of these, only the two .vscode files are touched by install.js at all, and that is the case worth being careful about, because they ARE written into every target. They are GENERATED, not copied: mergeSettings() builds the object in code key by key, and mergeTasks() calls buildTasks() from scripts/launcher/generate-tasks.js, which does ship (scripts/launcher goes wholesale). So the package having no source copy is correct.

The other five are this repository's own development and release apparatus — its CI workflow, its test suite, a probe script, a findings doc, and Pipeman's own verify-tarball.sh — none referenced by install.js as a path it reads. verify-tarball.sh is the interesting one: QA1's justification for shipping scripts/baselines wholesale is that verify-tarball.sh runs the UNPACKED tarball's check-staleness.js. That still holds with the script itself unshipped, because Pipeman runs it from the repo source against the tarball, not from inside it. Consistent, and I checked it rather than assuming.

BUT THE CODE READING IS NOT THE EVIDENCE. The installs below are.

================================================================
FRESH INSTALL — THE CRITERION THE ALLOWLIST MOST ENDANGERS: PASS
================================================================
`npx fully-completely@0.2.8` into a clean git repo. Completed, and produced every structure the criterion names:
  docs/sprints    7 phase dirs, 7 .gitkeep      scripts/launcher   12 files
  .claude/commands  15 files                    .claude/agents      6 files
  templates         1 file                      .vscode/settings.json + tasks.json (8 tasks), both generated

THEN THE PART THAT ACTUALLY ANSWERS THE RISK, because "the files are present" is not "the framework works". I ran the installed framework in the target:
  python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py list   -> works
  node scripts/run-lifecycle.js list         -> works
  sprint_lifecycle.py new "Fresh install probe" -> created docs/sprints/1-todo/sprint-1_...md from the shipped template
  sprint_lifecycle.py start 1                -> Phase: dev_build
  status 1                                   -> reads back correctly

A real sprint created and started end to end, from a fresh install of the new allowlist, using the shipped template. An under-inclusive array would have surfaced here — a missing template, a missing launcher module, a missing phase folder — and did not.

REGRESSION CHECK ON THE ONE PATH THAT LOOKED THIN. scripts/baselines installs 0 files into a target, which I did not want to assume was intended. Installed 0.2.7 into its own scratch repo to compare: 0.2.7 also puts 0 files there. Same in both, so this is not something 0.2.8 dropped — baselines is read from the package at install time, never installed. Checked against the previous release rather than reasoned about.

================================================================
UPGRADE, WITH BOTH PLANTS THE CRITERIA DEMAND: PASS
================================================================
Installed 0.2.7 into a clean repo, then planted what the criteria require to be planted rather than hoped for, then upgraded.

VERSION TRANSITION: "Upgraded 0.2.7 -> 0.2.8", first line, correct.

REQ 2 / 2a — the ignore rule merges, it does not overwrite. Before upgrading I appended two unrelated lines of my own ("my-secret-local-notes/", "*.myproj.tmp"). After:
  *.fc-bak-* present:              YES
  my-secret-local-notes/ survived: YES
  *.myproj.tmp survived:           YES

And I did not stop at "the line is in the file", because the requirement is about what git does, not what the file says:
  git check-ignore CLAUDE.md.fc-bak-0.1.9 -> .gitignore:7:*.fc-bak-*
  git status --ignored               -> all three backups listed as ignored
  git add -A, then count staged backups -> 0

THAT LAST LINE IS SPRINT 4'S DEFECT, CLOSED. The finding was that a downstream project running `git add -A` commits a backup carrying content someone had just scrubbed. I ran exactly that command against a target holding a backup carrying "Fifty Mission Cap" — the string sprint 22 scrubbed — and it staged nothing. The remediation that previously only looked complete now is.

REQ 3 / 3b — the report covers the population it exists for. I planted TWO backups from versions this run would never create (CLAUDE.md.fc-bak-0.1.9, .claude/agents/qa1.md.fc-bak-0.2.1). The report named both, alongside the one this run did create:

  "Backup files present, from any past upgrade (report only, nothing deleted) (3):
     .claude/agents/qa1.md.fc-bak-0.2.1
     CLAUDE.md.fc-bak-0.1.9
     scripts/install.js.fc-bak-0.2.7
   Each holds the PREVIOUS version's content from when it was replaced or removed. Safe to delete by
   hand once you are satisfied with the current version; nothing here removes them for you."

Both populations in one list. A run-scoped implementation would have shown only install.js.fc-bak-0.2.7 and missed exactly the long-upgraded projects Req 3b was written for. It doesn't.

REQ 3a — report only, proven by hash not by absence of a delete call. I recorded sha256 of both planted backups before the upgrade and re-checked after: both OK, byte-unchanged. "Fifty Mission Cap" still present, 1 occurrence, in the backup. Nothing deleted, nothing quietly scrubbed.

REQ 5 (LiveQA half) — no sprint data reached the target, checked independently of QA1's tarball work. The upgrade target I never touched holds exactly seven files under docs/sprints, all .gitkeep; no registry.json, no state/*.json, no sprint markdown. (My fresh-install target does contain a registry and a sprint-1 — those are the ones I created through the installed framework, not shipped ones, and I am naming that so the listing above is not misread.)

================================================================
ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A DEFECT
================================================================
My planted lines landed inside the existing managed block, so the installer appended a SECOND "# Fully Completely (added by scripts/install.js)" block for the new rule rather than rewriting around my lines. Two headers in one .gitignore looks untidy and I wanted to know whether blocks accumulate per install, which would be a real defect. They do not: I ran the installer three more times and it held at 2 headers and 1 fc-bak line throughout, reporting ".gitignore (already has the lines this framework needs)". A fresh install produces a single clean block with both rules. Cosmetic, idempotent, and the conservative behaviour is the right one — appending beats rewriting a file the user has edited. Recorded so nobody rediscovers it as a bug.

================================================================
WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
================================================================
Every result here came from real `npx` installs of published 0.2.8 into clean scratch git repos, not from reading package.json's array. The 63->56 drop I enumerated file by file and checked each against install.js rather than accepting "expected for this sprint" — Pipeman was right to flag it and right that structural checks passing is not the same test. The .vscode generation I confirmed by reading the two merge functions AND by observing both files appear in a target that received neither from the tarball. The gitignore result I took from git's own check-ignore and a real `git add -A`, not from grepping the file. The backup survival I took from sha256 before/after, not from the absence of a deletion in the output.

One correction to my own method: my first leak grep matched `sprint-*.md` and flagged the fifteen legitimate .claude/commands files and the template as leaks. That was my pattern being wrong, not the tarball being dirty; the authoritative check is the docs/sprints listing, which held only the seven .gitkeep. Recording it because a sloppy grep that over-reports is one bad glance away from a false FAIL.

CLOSED THIS ROUND: the package.json version-bump omission I have carried since sprint 30 is fixed — sprint 35's Req 4 states the bump explicitly, and adds "confirm that is still true at build time rather than trusting this line". Five sprints of re-flagging, resolved at the template level as QA1 said it should be.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================
Ship-ready. The allowlist is complete: a fresh install produces a framework that creates and starts a real sprint, and the seven files it stopped shipping are this repository's own apparatus, none of which install.js reads. Backups are now ignored by real git, reported whatever version created them, and left untouched on disk — which closes sprint 4's remediation in the only way that matters, since the defect there was that a scrub looked complete and wasn't.

Three items remain open from earlier gates, unchanged and none introduced here: the hollow-green CI case is still unobserved (though its sibling, the zero-runs refusal, fired live this round), /sprint-block and /sprint-abort still succeed on an already-complete sprint with no authorization, and the permission anchor is six CLI versions behind this machine.

This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 35.
